text:
maria: Heads-up — trying to bring up the new quantized Llama-13B build across clouds. seeing weirdly bifurcated warmstart behavior when we enable int8 prefix caching.

aj: Can you paste the p95 numbers you saw?

maria: quick summary: aws/us-east-1 (A100, driver 525.85) p95 ~ 41ms, gcp/us-central1 (A100, driver 525.89) p95 ~ 29ms, azure/westus2 (A100, driver 525.85) p95 ~ 68ms. all with same model/artifacts and identical bin.

devon: wow azure is way higher. are these cold-starts or warm KV cache runs?

maria: these are warmstart runs (we prefill KV cache with 512 tokens). int8 quant, batch=1, seq=512. throughput stable but tail worsens only on azure.

sana: any driver-level warnings in logs? cuda/cuDNN mismatch?

maria: azure nodes show repeated kernel fallback lines in the runtime log: `KernelSelector: fallback to generic_matmul_kernel for layer 23` and occasional `nvlink packet retry` spamming.

bench-bot: automated run summary: model=llama-13b quant=int8 warm_kv=1 runs=120 p50/p95/p99 (aws)=13/41/89ms (gcp)=12/29/71ms (azure)=14/68/160ms. full CSV uploaded to https://console.redwood.example/bench/runs/1956789012

aj: that NVLink retry log smells like firmware mismatch or interconnect congestion. what are the firmware and bios revisions on each provider?

maria: aws: fw 1.2.3. gcp: fw 1.2.5. azure: fw 1.1.9. also azure nodes are on an older microcode.

devon: older microcode could trigger different kernel selection heuristics in the driver leading to poorer occupancy. also could affect memcpy paths — therefore tail.

sana: could quantization amplify it? int8 kernels are more sensitive to block-size/warps. maybe on azure the driver picks a slower int8 GEMM kernel.

maria: I ran `rwd-bench run` locally with flags, here's the repro command we used: ```
# run a warm-start single-instance bench
rwd-bench run --model llama-13b --quant int8 --batch 1 --seq 512 --warm-kv --provider azure --region westus2 --runs 120 --out /tmp/azure-run.csv
```

aj: please also run the same with `--quant fp16` to see delta. if int8 delta huge, it's likely kernel selection.

maria: did that. fp16 p95 on azure drops to 33ms (close to gcp). so int8 is the offender.

devon: next steps: collect nsys trace for an int8 warm run on azure and on gcp, and compare the kernel names and grid/block dims. also get `nvidia-smi -q` outputs and `modinfo nvidia`/`cat /proc/driver/nvidia/version`.

sana: also check our runtime's kernel blacklist / fallback table. sometimes we ship heuristics that prefer a quant GEMM path only if driver reports certain capability bits. different microcode could flip that.

maria: good call. I'll fetch `modinfo` and nsys for one representative run and upload.

infra-bot: NOTE: scheduled maintenance on azure-westus2 NIC firmware on 1956796000. impact: possible reboots.

aj: timeline-wise, if maintenance hits it might transiently change numbers. try to snapshot current node images before the maintenance.

maria: uploaded traces + `nvidia-smi` outputs to the bench run link. key snippet from azure trace: `cuBlasLtMatmul_int8 -> generic_matmul_kernel` repeated; gcp shows `cuBlasLtMatmul_int8_fastpath`.

devon: confirms driver/kernel selection difference. for immediate mitigation: 1) force our runtime to use cuBLAS Lt path via env `RW_USE_CUBLASLT=1` 2) fallback to fp16 quant profile for azure customers 3) file a ticket with cloud partner to update microcode/firmware.

sana: can we detect this automatically and route requests to a compatible variant? e.g., if p95 > threshold for int8, route to fp16 model in that region.

aj: yes — add a runtime heuristic: if kernel_name contains `generic_matmul` or tail p95 > 2x baseline for 5% of samples, switch to a safe quant/profile. we already have routing policies, just need telemetry hooks.

maria: I'll open an eval PR with additional telemetry tags: kernel_name and matmul_latency. also add an experimental flag `--force-cublaslt` to rwd-bench so infra can test.

maria: one more weirdness — with int4 (experimental) azure p95 went even higher and instability increased. so skip int4 on azure until we fix driver/kernel.

devon: yep. create a short postmortem doc inside eng-ml notes with findings + mitigation. cc @sana for runtime heuristic implementation.

bench-bot: action items created: RB-4056 (collect nsys traces), RB-4057 (force-cublaslt bench), RB-4058 (routing heuristic), RB-4059 (partner firmware ticket).

maria: thanks. I'll run the `--force-cublaslt` bench and post results later today. anyone else want to try a repro before I start?

aj: I'll queue a gcp run to validate differences. ping me when traces uploaded. :thumbsup:

sana: I'll sketch the telemetry patch this afternoon.

maria: cool — will update here with results.
